# 0003: The code is the source of the source texts

**Context.** `Rcinel.Translate("id", "English text")` puts the English text in the code. Keeping a
second copy in a source file by hand would drift.

**Decision.** `translations/<source>.json` is generated by `rcinel scan`, which collects the calls
(like xgettext). The editor never edits the source language. A call with an empty id gets one from
`scan --assign`, written back into the code file. The English text in the call is also the runtime
fallback, so an untranslated string shows English and the app needs no source file at all.

**Alternatives.** *Edit English in the editor*: then code and file disagree, and the code wins at
runtime anyway. *Resource-file workflows* (keys in code, texts in .resx): the texts are no longer
where they are used.

**Consequences.** The scanner must read the call, so id and text must be plain string literals;
anything else is reported. Translations of ids that disappear stay until `rcinel prune`, so a revert
doesn't lose them.

Related: [[0001-uuidv7-keys-sorted-by-time]]
